thread:
alyssa: FYI found a discrepancy in the route dashboard billing attribution. Console-run requests are showing up billed to the service account project instead of the project shown in the console UI. Customers will be confused.

vikram: That rings a bell. Console does an exchange token for impersonation which includes sa and org claims. Our emitter currently prefers `sa` claim for project attribution.

dan: Quick question: is the console also sending an `effective_project` header? I thought we added that some time ago.

alyssa: Yes, console sets `X-Effective-Project` with the intended billing project. But the metrics pipeline ignores that header and picks `sa` project from the token.

elaine: Oops. We designed the emitter to be conservative and only use token claims, but you're right that's wrong for console intent. Two fixes: (A) change emitter to prefer `X-Effective-Project` if present; (B) post-process at billing to remap based on console logs.

vikram: I prefer (A) because it's explicit and immediate. (B) is opaque and harder to guarantee for sampled telemetry. But we need validation: `X-Effective-Project` could be malformed.

dan: If we change emitter, we must gate it behind a feature flag and add metrics so we can detect bad or unknown effective_project values.

alyssa: Proposal: emitter priority = effective_project -> service_account_project -> org_project. Feature-flag rollout: CANARY in staging, then 24h canary in prod, then ramp.

ops-bot: deploy: feature/attr-prefer-effective_project toggled to CANARY in staging at 1719409900.

vikram: I'll implement emitter change + validation against project index. If the effective project lookup fails we set `attribution_source=unknown` and emit a counter `effective_project_validation_fail`.

elaine: We'll also add `attribution_fallback_reason` with values: `effective_project`, `service_account`, `org`, `unknown` so dashboards can show if we are falling back.

dan: UX side: add a small label on route/details: "Billed to proj_123 (via console intent)" with hover text: "Attributed from effective_project header. token_origin=proj_x". That should reduce support noise.

alyssa: Also need to think about cross-org SA cases: user in Org A runs as proj X but SA belongs to Org B. We must decide charge semantics: console intent should probably win for predictability, but legal may want explicit consent for cross-org billing.

dan: Good point. Add both fields to exports: `billing_project` (what we bill) and `token_origin_project`. Legal asked for both for audits.

sre-jen: Important: quota enforcement uses the key in the token. If we switch billing_project attribution only, quota alerts will look mismatched. Add separate metrics: `requests_enforced_by` vs `requests_billed_to` so alerts stay meaningful.

elaine: And add a nightly reconciliation job that compares billing vs quota for the first week after rollout and flags deltas > 5%.

vikram: Implementation steps I propose: 1) change emitter logic behind flag, 2) validate effective_project via project index, 3) emit attribution_fallback_reason + validation_fail metric, 4) add billing_project & token_origin_project to exports, 5) update dashboards and console label, 6) run canary and reconciliation. I'll own 1-3 and 5.

alyssa: I'll own coordination with product and legal, write the support blurb and console copy. Dan can update export formats and docs. Elaine will wire up metrics/dashboards and the reconciliation job.

ops-bot: audit: change recorded by alyssa at 1719409945.

dan: Timeline? Can we get staging CANARY today and prod ramp tomorrow if no issues?

vikram: I'll open the PR now, aim to merge in 2 hours. If tests are green I'll flip the staging flag and run canary.

alyssa: Great. We'll watch `attribution_fallback_reason` and `billing_vs_quota_delta` for 72h post-ramp. If anything odd, revert flag.

ops-bot: alert rule added: `billing_vs_quota_delta > 0.05` -> notify #eng-platform-canary at 1719409988.

elaine: tiny nit: please make header name `X-Effective-Project` canonical and document it in the internal API spec so other producers use the same header.

alyssa: Will do. Thanks all.
